key_insight: Environment-assisted imaginary time evolution helps FALQON escape stagnation and reach ground states in simulated quantum optimization problems.
engineering_relevance: Combining environmental quantum operations with feedback control could reduce circuit-layer requirements without classical parameter optimization.
method: Represent imaginary time evolution as a quantum operation induced by an environment.
Combine this operation with the FALQON feedback law in CITE-FALQON.
Simulate ground-state preparation for a frustrated ANNNI Ising chain and MaxCut.
evidence_signal: For the two simulated problems, CITE-FALQON reached ground states from any initial state and used fewer layers on average in fixed-initial-state comparisons, including cases where FALQON failed.
watch_item: Hardware feasibility remains to be established, and the advantage depends strongly on the ANNNI phase and MaxCut graph weights.
paper_title: Environment-assisted imaginary time evolution in feedback-based quantum algorithms
